---
title: "About"
---

This is the course site for **Dynamics & Simulation** (AKA Intermediate
Dynamics, ME 4730/5730), taught by [Prof. Andy Ruina](https://ruina.org) at
Plaksha University, reusing the Cornell lecture recordings.

The site is a static [Quarto](https://quarto.org) website. Everything on the
Lectures and Homework pages is generated at build time from a single
spreadsheet plus the folders of PDFs — there is no database and no backend.

## How to update this site

Adding a year of videos, a new set of lecture notes, or a new set of solutions
is a **spreadsheet + folder** change. It should never need a code change.

### 1. Edit `Dynamics&Sim-MasterSheet.xlsx`

This file is the source of truth. Two sheets:

**`Lectures`** — one row per lecture.

| Column | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Lec No.`, `Name of Lecture` | Fixed identity columns. |
| `Link (YYYY)` | A set of video links. The label shown on the site is whatever is inside the parentheses. Add a whole new year by adding a new column, e.g. `Link (2027)`. A cell may hold more than one URL. |
| Any other column | A **notes set**. The header must match a folder name under `Notes/` exactly. Each cell holds the note number(s) covering that lecture. |

Notes cells accept `7`, `16, 17`, or `03, 04 -> some commentary` (the trailing
commentary becomes a tooltip). Leave a cell blank for "no notes".

**`Homeworks`** — one row per problem.

| Column | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Homework No. (Plaksha Doc)` | Fixed identity column. Must match the problem numbering inside the combined homework PDF. |
| `Done Last Time (...)` | Usage history — `y` or `n`. Add another column, e.g. `Done Last Time (2027 Plaksha)`, to track another offering. |
| Any other column | A **solutions set**. The header must match a folder name under `Homework/` exactly. Each cell holds the solution code, e.g. `Q01`. |

::: {.callout-important}
Excel sometimes autocorrects an entry like `9, 10` into a date. If it does,
format the cell as **Text** and retype the value — otherwise the build will
warn and skip that cell.
:::

### 2. Add the matching folder

For a new notes or solutions set, create a folder under `Notes/` or
`Homework/` **named exactly like the new column header**, and drop the files
in it.

- **Notes files** are matched by their leading number: `7. Whatever.pdf`,
  `07 Whatever.pdf` and `Lecture 07 Whatever.pdf` all resolve to note 7. One
  file can cover several notes (`Lecture 09 10 ....pdf`).
- **Solution files** are matched by their code prefix: `Q01...pdf`. A solution
  may live in a same-named subfolder alongside supporting `.m`/`.png` files,
  which get listed with it.
- A filename or folder containing any of the keywords below is flagged with a
  ⚠ "not instructor-reviewed" badge. Punctuation and capitalisation are
  ignored when matching, so `Not Approved` and `NotApproved` both count. Edit
  `UNAPPROVED_KEYWORDS` at the top of `scripts/build_data.py` to change the
  list — this page reads it from there, so it cannot go stale:

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "scripts")
from build_data import UNAPPROVED_KEYWORDS

print("  " + ", ".join(f"`{k}`" for k in UNAPPROVED_KEYWORDS))
```
- Anything left over in a solutions folder that no row references is still
  published, under "Other materials" on the Homework page.

### 3. Render locally to check

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
quarto render
```

The pre-render step regenerates `_data/` and prints warnings for anything it
could not resolve — an unparseable cell, a missing note file, a solution code
with no matching PDF. Read those warnings; they are how you catch typos.

Use `quarto preview` for a live-reloading local copy.

### 4. Commit and push

```bash
git add -A && git commit -m "Update course materials" && git push
```

GitHub Actions rebuilds and redeploys the site automatically on every push to
`main`.

## How it fits together

- `scripts/build_data.py` — pre-render step. Reads the spreadsheet, scans
  `Notes/` and `Homework/`, resolves every reference to a real file, works out
  which page of the combined PDF each problem starts on, and writes JSON into
  `_data/`.
- `scripts/coursesite.py` — small helpers the pages use to turn that JSON into
  links and badges.
- `lectures.qmd` / `homework.qmd` — read the JSON and render it with
  [itables](https://mwouts.github.io/itables/), which gives client-side
  sorting, searching and paging on a fully static page.
- `_data/` and `files/` are generated on every render and are not checked in.

The site is intentionally public — there is no login.
